C1 | 00:00 | intro: the topic of the video is finger strength without injuries
C2 | 01:40 | leave at least 48 hours between two hard finger sessions
C3 | 01:47 | the days in between are for easy mileage on big holds
C4 | 03:10 | after about six weeks most people add one grade (prediction)
C5 | 03:40 | no one-arm hangs before 20 seconds two-armed on the 20 millimeter edge
C6 | 04:05 | a fourth session in the off-season is an option

# Tomas Brink Advises His Athletes To Leave At Least 48 Hours Between Two Hard Finger Sessions

Tomas Brink tells his athletes to leave at least 48 hours between two hard finger sessions. [src: vid-EXAMPLE0002 @ 01:40]

## Details

- He tells his athletes to leave at least 48 hours between two hard finger sessions. [src: vid-EXAMPLE0002 @ 01:40]
- The days in between are for easy mileage on big holds. [src: vid-EXAMPLE0002 @ 01:47]

## Evidence

- vid-EXAMPLE0002 @ 01:40 (Tomas Brink): "I tell my athletes to leave at least 48 hours between two hard finger sessions."
- vid-EXAMPLE0002 @ 01:47 (Tomas Brink): "The days in between are for easy mileage on big holds."

# Tomas Brink Requires 20 Seconds Two-Armed On The 20 Millimeter Edge Before One-Arm Hangs

Tomas Brink says not to start one-arm hangs until you can hold 20 seconds two-armed on the 20 millimeter edge. [src: vid-EXAMPLE0002 @ 03:40]

## Details

- Do not start one-arm hangs until you can hold 20 seconds two-armed on the 20 millimeter edge. [src: vid-EXAMPLE0002 @ 03:40]

## Evidence

- vid-EXAMPLE0002 @ 03:40 (Tomas Brink): "Do not start one-arm hangs until you can hold 20 seconds two-armed on the 20 millimeter edge."
